# ym command reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m yourls_manager.clidoc` from the help texts in cli.py. Do not edit. -->

Manage a Git-tracked YOURLS site: vendor core and plugins, build, deploy.

## Global options

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--version` | show program's version number and exit |
| `--site-dir PATH` | site repo directory (default: search upward from cwd for site.toml) |
| `-v, --verbose` | verbose output |

```
exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   error
  2   usage or configuration error
  10  updates available (update --check, plugin list --check)
```

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| [`ym core`](#ym-core) | vendor YOURLS core at a tag |
| [`ym build`](#ym-build) | assemble dist/ from yourls/ + overlay/ |
| [`ym deploy`](#ym-deploy) | build and deploy to a target |
| [`ym verify`](#ym-verify) | health check + redirect tests |

| [`ym artifact`](#ym-artifact) | release archives for sites ym doesn't deploy: build |

| [`ym repo`](#ym-repo) | store the site on GitHub or GitLab (create the repo/project, push) |

| [`ym init`](#ym-init) | interactive wizard: new site or adopt an existing install (resumable) |

## ym core

Vendor YOURLS core at a tag.

```
ym core [--dry-run] [--force] [VERSION]
```

Fetch YOURLS core at a tag and replace yourls/, keeping the managed plugin directories and applying [core].exclude. Updates the lock and [core].version. Refuses when yourls/ has uncommitted changes (Git is the backup) unless --force.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `VERSION` | tag to vendor, or 'latest' (default: site.toml [core].version) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | show what would change, then stop |
| `--force` | ignore uncommitted changes in yourls/ |

## ym build

Assemble dist/ from yourls/ + overlay/.

```
ym build [--out DIR] [--allow-drift]
```

Clean the output directory, then copy yourls/ and overlay/ into it (overlay wins; -v lists each override). Refuses when yourls/ doesn't match the lock.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--out DIR` | output dir (default: [build].out) |
| `--allow-drift` | build even if yourls/ differs from the lock |

## ym deploy

Build and deploy to a target.

```
ym deploy [--dry-run] [--no-build] [--skip-verify]
          [--allow-dirty] [--force] [--skip-backup] [--verify-remote]
          target
```

rsync targets: build, preflight, DB backup, rsync, DB upgrade, plugins, verify. sftp targets: build, upload changed files, delete files ym deployed before, then print the browser steps (install/upgrade, plugins) and verify. Refuses uncommitted changes unless --allow-dirty; a target with accept = "release" only takes a commit with a final release tag. Afterwards the local branch deployed/<target> points at the deployed commit.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | target name ([deploy.targets.NAME] in site.toml) |

**All targets**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | show what would change, then stop |
| `--no-build` | deploy the existing build output |
| `--skip-verify` | do not run verify afterwards |
| `--allow-dirty` | deploy even with uncommitted changes |
| `--force` | override the target's accept = "release" policy (recorded in release.json) |

**Rsync targets**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--skip-backup` | do not dump the database first (sftp targets never back it up) |

**Sftp targets**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--verify-remote` | stat every deployed file and re-upload the ones changed on the server |

## ym verify

Health check + redirect tests.

```
ym verify [--url URL] [target]
```

GET /health.php (expects {"ok": true}), then check each case in tests/redirects.toml. Redirects are not followed.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | target whose url to check |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--url URL` | base URL to check instead of a target's url |

## ym plugin

Plugins: search, add, remove, list, enable, disable, sync, apply.

```
ym plugin ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym plugin list` | plugins in site.toml: version, source, lock, updates |
| `ym plugin sync` | vendor plugins into yourls/user/plugins (locked commits; --update: newest) |
| `ym plugin apply` | make the target's active plugins exactly site.toml's |
| `ym plugin search` | search the awesome-yourls plugin catalog |
| `ym plugin add` | add a plugin by catalog name or git/project URL |
| `ym plugin remove` | remove a plugin from the site |
| `ym plugin enable` | enable a plugin in site.toml |
| `ym plugin disable` | disable a plugin in site.toml |

### ym plugin list

Plugins in site.toml: version, source, lock, updates.

```
ym plugin list [--json] [--check]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |
| `--check` | ask upstream for newer commits (exit 10 if any) |

### ym plugin sync

Vendor plugins into yourls/user/plugins (locked commits; --update: newest).

```
ym plugin sync [--update] [--dry-run] [--force] [NAME ...]
```

Vendor the site.toml plugins that have a repo into yourls/user/plugins/<name>, at the locked commit while repo/ref/path are unchanged. --update re-resolves refs. A managed plugin removed from site.toml has its directory deleted.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | only these plugins (default: all) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--update` | re-resolve refs to latest commits |
| `--dry-run` | show what would change, then stop |
| `--force` | ignore uncommitted changes in yourls/ |

### ym plugin apply

Make the target's active plugins exactly site.toml's.

```
ym plugin apply target
```

rsync targets: activate and deactivate plugins with the PHP helper so the active set is exactly the plugins marked active in site.toml (deploy does this too). sftp targets have no PHP CLI: this prints what to change in the admin UI.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | target name |

### ym plugin search

Search the awesome-yourls plugin catalog.

```
ym plugin search [--category SLUG] [--refresh] [--json]
                 [query ...]
```

Search the awesome-yourls catalog (cached for a day in ~/.cache/yourls-manager/; $XDG_CACHE_HOME is honored) by name, tags and description (name matches rank first). Plugins already in site.toml are marked. --category alone lists a category. Works outside a site repo.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `query` | search words (all must match) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--category SLUG` | limit to a category (lists it alone) |
| `--refresh` | download the catalog again |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |

### ym plugin add

Add a plugin by catalog name or git/project URL.

```
ym plugin add [--name NAME] [--ref REF] [--path PATH]
              [--inactive] [--no-sync] [--refresh]
              NAME|URL
```

Add a plugin by its awesome-yourls catalog name (exact, case-insensitive or unique prefix; quote names with spaces) or by a clone URL / project page (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Bitbucket; /tree/<ref>/<dir> sets ref and path). plugin.php is looked for at the top of the repo, else one directory down (several: asks on a terminal, else needs --path). Shows the plugin header, appends a [[plugins]] block to site.toml and vendors it. Refuses duplicates and directory names used by core or overlay/. Catalog entries that link to a web page need the repo URL instead.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME\|URL` | catalog name or git/project URL |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name NAME` | plugin directory name (default: from plugin.php's folder) |
| `--ref REF` | branch, tag or commit (default: from the URL, else HEAD) |
| `--path PATH` | subdirectory holding plugin.php |
| `--inactive` | add it with active = false |
| `--no-sync` | only edit site.toml; vendor later with ym plugin sync |
| `--refresh` | download the catalog again |

### ym plugin remove

Remove a plugin from the site.

```
ym plugin remove [--keep-files] name
```

Delete the plugin's [[plugins]] block from site.toml and its vendored copy (refused if that copy has uncommitted changes). The next deploy deactivates it and removes its files; plugin data (options, tables) stays in the database.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | plugin directory name, as in site.toml |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--keep-files` | keep the vendored copy |

### ym plugin enable

Enable a plugin in site.toml.

```
ym plugin enable name
```

Set active = true in the plugin's site.toml block (comments kept). The next deploy applies it.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | plugin directory name, as in site.toml |

### ym plugin disable

Disable a plugin in site.toml.

```
ym plugin disable name
```

Set active = false in the plugin's site.toml block (comments kept). The next deploy applies it.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | plugin directory name, as in site.toml |

## ym update

Update core and plugins to their newest versions and build (--check: report only).

```
ym update [--commit] [--core-only | --plugins-only] [--force]
          [--check] [--json]
```

Update core to the newest stable release and plugins to their newest commits, build, and summarize the lock changes. --check is read-only: it asks upstream with git ls-remote (skipping -rc/-beta core tags) and exits 10 if anything can be updated.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--commit` | commit the update with a summary |
| `--core-only` | only update YOURLS core |
| `--plugins-only` | only update plugins |
| `--force` | ignore uncommitted changes in yourls/ |
| `--check` | only report what can be updated (read-only; exit 10 if anything can) |
| `--json` | with --check: machine-readable output |

## ym release

Tag a release: v<yourls>-<rev>[-rc.<n>]; list, promote.

```
ym release [--rc] [--push] [--dry-run] [-m MESSAGE] ACTION ...
```

Without an action: tag the next release v<yourls>-<rev> (--rc: -rc.<n>) on a clean, drift-free tree, with release notes from the lock diff.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--rc` | tag a release candidate |
| `--push` | push the new tag to origin |
| `--dry-run` | show the tag and notes only |
| `-m, --message MESSAGE` | extra text for the release notes |

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym release promote` | tag the newest rc's commit as its final release |
| `ym release list` | releases, their dates, and where each is deployed |

### ym release promote

Tag the newest rc's commit as its final release.

```
ym release promote [--push] [--dry-run] [-m MESSAGE]
```

Tag the newest rc's commit as its final release: vX-N-rc.k -> vX-N.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--push` | push the new tag to origin |
| `--dry-run` | show the tag and notes only |
| `-m, --message MESSAGE` | extra text for the release notes |

### ym release list

Releases, their dates, and where each is deployed.

```
ym release list
```

## ym artifact

Release archives for sites ym doesn't deploy: build.

```
ym artifact ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym artifact build` | build a release tag into reproducible .tar.gz/.zip files with sha256 + metadata |

### ym artifact build

Build a release tag into reproducible .tar.gz/.zip files with sha256 + metadata.

```
ym artifact build [--ref REF] [--out DIR] [--format F]
                  [--allow-untagged]
```

Build the web root of a release tag (REF must carry v<yourls>-<rev>[-rc.<n>]; the tree must be clean) and write it as archives without a top-level directory, a <archive>.sha256 per archive and one <name>.json with the release metadata. Rebuilding a tag gives byte-identical archives. Nothing is uploaded.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--ref REF` | release tag or commit to build (default: HEAD) |
| `--out DIR` | output directory (default: [build].out + '-artifacts', e.g. dist-artifacts/) |
| `--format F` | tar.gz or zip (repeatable; default: [artifact].formats) |
| `--allow-untagged` | local testing only: build an untagged commit as version 0.0.0-dev+<sha> |

## ym doctor

Read-only health report: tools, site repo, targets (exit 1 on failures).

```
ym doctor [--local] [target]
```

Check local tools, site.toml, the lock and drift, uncommitted and unpushed changes, and per target: login, PHP CLI (rsync), server config, https url, install/upgrade state, and the deployed commit vs HEAD. With [artifact] enabled = true, also that a CI job publishes the artifacts. Changes nothing. --local skips the targets (offline) and exits 1 on drift.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | check only this target (default: all) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--local` | only tools and the site repo (no network) |

## ym repo

Store the site on GitHub or GitLab (create the repo/project, push).

```
ym repo ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym repo create` | create the site's repo as origin and push the current branch (needs gh or glab) |

### ym repo create

Create the site's repo as origin and push the current branch (needs gh or glab).

```
ym repo create [--name NAME] [--owner OWNER] [--host HOST]
               [--public] [--dry-run]
```

Create a repository for this site (private unless --public), add it as origin (or create the one origin already names), and push the current branch. Tags are not pushed. Nothing about deploying changes: that stays manual unless you run `ym ci setup`. Where: GitHub with the GitHub CLI (gh), or GitLab with the GitLab CLI (glab) on sites made with ci_provider = gitlab; there the project comes from origin, else the template's repo_url answer, else --host/--owner/--name, and self-managed GitLab works through --host.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name NAME` | repository name (default: the site directory name) |
| `--owner OWNER` | user, organization or group path (default: your login) |
| `--host HOST` | GitLab host (default: gitlab.com; GitLab sites only) |
| `--public` | create it public (default: private) |
| `--dry-run` | show what would be created |

## ym ci

Deploy from GitHub Actions or GitLab CI (opt-in per target): setup, status.

```
ym ci ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym ci setup` | enable CI deploys: environment, CI key, host keys, ci = true (gh or glab) |
| `ym ci status` | check the CI environments and secrets of ci = true targets (exit 1 if not ready) |

### ym ci setup

Enable CI deploys: environment, CI key, host keys, ci = true (gh or glab).

```
ym ci setup [--repo OWNER/NAME] [--rotate] [--skip-updates]
            [--dry-run]
            [TARGET ...]
```

Enable deploys from the site template's CI file (.github/workflows/deploy.yml with the GitHub CLI, or .gitlab-ci.yml with the GitLab CLI on ci_provider = gitlab sites): create the environment (prod -> production, other targets -> staging), generate a dedicated CI key, install it on the server over your working login, check it logs in, store it as DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, store the host keys from ~/.ssh/known_hosts as DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS, and set `ci = true` on the target in site.toml. GitLab: File-type, protected variables scoped to the environment, and the v* tags are protected. Offers the CLI's login, and `ym repo create` when the site has no repository yet. GitLab also sets up check-updates (unless --skip-updates): the weekly pipeline schedule `ym check-updates` and the masked variable YM_UPDATE_TOKEN the job pushes with (a project access token; when GitLab refuses to create one, e.g. on a free gitlab.com namespace, it asks you to paste a token with write_repository). This works without deploy targets, e.g. on artifact-only sites.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `TARGET` | default: prod and staging |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--repo OWNER/NAME` | GitHub repo or GitLab project (default: from the remote) |
| `--rotate` | replace an existing DEPLOY_SSH_KEY (and YM_UPDATE_TOKEN) |
| `--skip-updates` | GitLab: don't set up the check-updates schedule and token |
| `--dry-run` | show what would be set, change nothing |

```
examples:
  ym ci setup                 # prod, staging and targets with ci = true
  ym ci setup prod --dry-run
  ym ci setup prod --rotate   # replace the CI key (and offer to remove the old one)
```

### ym ci status

Check the CI environments and secrets of ci = true targets (exit 1 if not ready).

```
ym ci status [TARGET ...]
```

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `TARGET` | default: targets with ci = true |

## ym target

Deploy targets: add, list, log in, write the server-local config.

```
ym target ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym target add` | add a deploy target to site.toml |
| `ym target list` | show the deploy targets in site.toml |
| `ym target login` | check that ym can log in to a target; set up an SSH key if needed |
| `ym target config` | create the server-local YOURLS config (secrets) on a target |

### ym target add

Add a deploy target to site.toml.

```
ym target add [--type {rsync,sftp}] [--host HOST] [--user USER]
              [--port PORT] [--path PATH] [--php PHP] [--url URL] [--accept {any,release}]
              [--protect PATH]
              NAME
```

Append a [deploy.targets.NAME] block to site.toml (comments are kept; the file is restored if the result doesn't validate). On a terminal ym asks for what isn't given; otherwise --path is required (and --host for sftp). Without --host an rsync target deploys on this machine. The prod target defaults to accept = "release".

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | target name, e.g. prod or staging |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--type {rsync,sftp}` | default: rsync |
| `--host HOST` | server host name (omit for a local rsync target) |
| `--user USER` | login user (default: ~/.ssh/config or your local user) |
| `--port PORT` | SSH/SFTP port (default: 22) |
| `--path PATH` | web root, relative to the login directory or absolute |
| `--php PHP` | rsync targets: PHP CLI on the server (default: php) |
| `--url URL` | public URL on this target (default: [site].url) |
| `--accept {any,release}` | deploy policy (default: "release" for prod, else "any") |
| `--protect PATH` | remote path deploys never delete (repeatable; default: .well-known/) |

### ym target list

Show the deploy targets in site.toml.

```
ym target list [--json]
```

Each target's type, location, url, deploy policy and whether CI deploys it.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |

### ym target login

Check that ym can log in to a target; set up an SSH key if needed.

```
ym target login [--key PATH] target
```

ym logs in non-interactively, so a target needs a login that works without prompts. rsync targets: SSH key authentication (BatchMode). If it fails, this creates a key with ssh-keygen when there is none and installs it with ssh-copy-id (asking for the SSH password once; plain ssh where ssh-copy-id is missing), then checks again. It explains the fix when a passphrase-protected key isn't in an agent (ssh-add) or a non-default key needs an ~/.ssh/config entry. sftp targets: the check is an SFTP login (SFTP-only accounts have no shell). A key is optional there: a password in $YM_<TARGET>_PASSWORD works too. To install a key, ym logs in with the password once and appends it to .ssh/authorized_keys over SFTP.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | target name |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--key PATH` | private key path (default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) |

### ym target config

Create the server-local YOURLS config (secrets) on a target.

```
ym target config [--force] [--from-existing] [--db-host H]
                 [--db-name N] [--db-user U] [--db-prefix P] [--admin-user U]
                 target
```

Write the target's config_file (mode 0600) from server/config.example.php: DB settings, YOURLS_SITE (the target's url), a fresh cookie key and one admin user whose password is hashed by the target's PHP (sftp targets: locally with bcrypt). With --from-existing, copy the existing install's user/config.php instead (when adopting).

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | target name |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--force` | replace an existing file (kept as .bak-<UTC>) |
| `--from-existing` | copy <web root>/user/config.php (or includes/config.php) to config_file |
| `--db-host H` | YOURLS_DB_HOST (default: example's value) |
| `--db-name N` | YOURLS_DB_NAME (prompted if omitted) |
| `--db-user U` | YOURLS_DB_USER (prompted if omitted) |
| `--db-prefix P` | YOURLS_DB_PREFIX (default: yourls_) |
| `--admin-user U` | admin username (prompted if omitted) |

```
secrets (never pass them as arguments):
  YM_DB_PASSWORD      database password (else prompted)
  YM_ADMIN_PASSWORD   admin password (else prompted twice)
```

## ym new

Create a site repo from the template (copier), vendor core + plugins, git init.

```
ym new [--template SRC] [--vcs-ref REF] [--data K=V] [--defaults]
       [--no-vendor] [--no-git]
       [DEST]
```

Create a new site repo from yourls-site-template with Copier (run as `uvx copier`), then vendor YOURLS core and plugins (ym core + ym plugin sync), best-effort `uv lock`, and make the initial git commit (skipped with a warning when no Git identity is set). Copier asks its questions unless --defaults. DEST must be empty or not exist.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `DEST` | new site directory |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--template SRC` | template (path, git URL or gh:owner/repo) |
| `--vcs-ref REF` | template git ref (default: its latest release tag) |
| `--data K=V` | answer a template question (repeatable), e.g. site_url=https://go.example.com |
| `--defaults` | use defaults for unanswered questions |
| `--no-vendor` | skip `ym core` + `ym plugin sync` |
| `--no-git` | skip git init and the initial commit |

```
examples:
  ym new go-example-com
  ym new go-example-com --defaults --data site_name='Example Go Links' \
      --data site_url=https://go.example.com
environment:
  YM_TEMPLATE   template source used when --template is not given
                (default: gh:RubenFixit/yourls-site-template)
```

## ym template

The site template (yourls-site-template): update.

```
ym template ACTION ...
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `ym template update` | pull template changes into this site repo (copier update) |

### ym template update

Pull template changes into this site repo (copier update).

```
ym template update [--vcs-ref REF] [--manager-version vX.Y.Z]
                   [--defaults] [--data K=V]
```

Run `copier update` in a clean site repo, then best-effort `uv lock`, and show what changed. Previously answered questions are not asked again.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--vcs-ref REF` | template git ref (default: latest tag) |
| `--manager-version vX.Y.Z` | pin this yourls-manager tag in pyproject.toml (manager_version answer) |
| `--defaults` | accept defaults for new questions |
| `--data K=V` | change an answer (repeatable), e.g. ci_provider=gitlab or release_artifact=true |

## ym adopt

Bring an existing YOURLS install under management.

```
ym adopt (--from-target TARGET | --from-dir PATH) [--ignore GLOB]
         [--active A,B,...] [--dry-run]
```

Snapshot an existing install, vendor core at its version, copy site-specific files and plugins into overlay/ (collisions with template files go to adopt-review/), add [[plugins]] entries, and check build/install parity. Writes adopt-review/REPORT.md. Run inside a site repo created by `ym new`. sftp targets: the active plugins can't be read; give them with --active, or answer the per-plugin prompt (on a terminal).

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--from-target TARGET` | pull the target's web root |
| `--from-dir PATH` | a local copy of the install |
| `--ignore GLOB` | extra path glob to ignore (repeatable; added to the defaults) |
| `--active A,B,...` | plugins active on the install (comma-separated; '' for none); instead of reading them from its database |
| `--dry-run` | analyze and print the plan only |

## ym init

Interactive wizard: new site or adopt an existing install (resumable).

```
ym init [DIR]
```

Guided onboarding (needs a terminal). Prints each equivalent command. Progress is saved, so running it again after an error resumes where it stopped.

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `DIR` | site repo to resume |
